meaning: The form you submit to pick your elective subjects for the semester. Skip it and the college assigns defaults for you.
Official permission that marks you 'present' even though you're away for a college-approved event, so it doesn't count against your attendance.
Official forgiveness for low attendance (usually 65-75%). Without it you may be blocked from sitting the semester exam.
A subject you failed or didn't clear. You get a supplementary exam to clear it instead of waiting a full year.
You're allowed to move to the next year/semester even with a pending backlog, as long as it's within the allowed limit.
Your overall academic score across all semesters combined, usually on a 10-point scale.
Your grade point average for just one semester, not your whole degree.
The official college web portal for attendance, grades, fees, forms and circulars — basically the one login that runs everything administrative.
A government portal for applying to and tracking scholarships. Needs document verification before money is released.
An absence that's been officially excused after you submit proof, so it no longer counts against your attendance percentage.
A retake exam offered after the main exam, usually for students clearing a backlog.
Blocked from writing the semester exam because your attendance percentage is too low and wasn't condoned in time.
